newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Schneider charged with fraud in Germany.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Schneider charged with fraud in Germany.

text.p: The Frankfurt prosecutor's office said on Monday it had filed fraud charges against former property tycoon Juergen Schneider in connection with the collapse of his real estate empire in 1994.

The office said it had charged Schneider on December 17 with credit fraud in two cases, serious fraud in three cases and with one case of bankruptcy. The charges carry a maximum sentence of 15 years in prison.

Schneider, once one of Germany's most celebrated entrepreneurs, fell from grace when he and his wife vanished in April 1994, leaving their company to crumble under more than 5 billion marks ($3.2 billion) of debt.
The Schneiders were detained in Miami in 1995 after a year-long international manhunt. They returned voluntarily to Germany last February to face questioning. He is being held in a Frankfurt prison.
Prosecutors allege he obtained credit from banks under false pretences, such as by overstating his rental income and presenting forged bills.
They also allege he contributed to the bankruptcy of his group by transferring 245 million marks to Switzerland.

Schneider's disappearance in April 1994 as his empire collapsed, and later the bankruptcy of his group, exposed his creditor banks to public outrage at the apparent ease with which he obtained funding from them.
His lawyers said on Sunday Schneider was committed to fighting the allegations and that his creditor banks were responsible for the bankruptcy.
But prosecutors said they had found no evidence of any wrongdoing by banks, led by Deutsche Bank AG, his biggest creditor.
"In the investigation so far we have found no indications that criminal acts were conducted in the banks," Frankfurt prosecutor Dieter Haike told a news conference. "But mistakes were made."
The prosecutor's office also said that Schneider's wife Claudia had been charged with bankruptcy and that a Schneider associate, Karl-Heinrich Kuepferle, had been charged with abetting fraud.
Claudia Schneider has been conditionally freed from detention because of concern for her health. ($1=1.5492 Mark)
